summary: Say the counting numbers in order, from 1 all the way up to 20.
Show how many are in a group with a written number from 0 to 12, using 0 for none.
Start counting from a number other than 1, like 4, and keep going (starting under 10).
Know that the last number said when counting tells how many things there are.
Count objects by touching each one once while saying the numbers in order.
Know a group has the same number of things whatever order they are counted in.
Count to say how many: up to 10 in a line, array or circle, or up to 5 scattered.
Tell if one group has more, fewer or the same number as another group, up to 10.
See how many are in a small group, up to 5, at a glance without counting.
Compare two written numbers from 1 to 5 and say which one is more.
Add and take away with objects or fingers, or by acting out everyday situations.
Split a number up to 5 into two parts in more than one way, using objects.
Notice patterns in everyday things around them and in numbers.
Describe and compare things by how long, big, full or heavy they are.
Put two things side by side to see which is longer, heavier or holds more.
Sort things into groups, count each group (up to 10), and say which group has more.
Gather information by sorting things into groups to answer a simple question.
Name squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, cubes, cones, cylinders and balls at any size or turn.
Name the shapes of things around them and say where things are, using position words.
Compare flat and solid shapes of different sizes and turns, and talk about their parts.
Make shapes while playing, by building them with blocks or drawing them.
Put several shapes together to make a picture or fill a simple outline puzzle.
